scoring_justification: Checker recomputes plateau magnetizations from the raw simulation output and compares to paper-reported plateau values, ensuring the simulation reproduces the correct spin states. Critical crystal fields are compared to paper values with tolerance ±1.0.

hidden_assets.purpose: Hidden gold: paper-reported critical crystal fields and plateau magnetization ranges/values. These are embedded in the checker to prevent information leakage.
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Extracted from the paper (Section 'Results and Discussion', description of Fig. 4).
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: These are the exact values reported by the authors; the reference solution writes them, and a genuine reproduction will produce values within tolerance.

schema.description: Raw magnetization data showing plateau structure.

outputs.description: Magnetization values of the Mn sublattice as a function of reduced crystal field for two Nd-Mn exchange strengths.

schema.description: Two lines: first line for R1=0.5 with three comma-separated floats (d_sc1,d_sc2,d_sc3); second line for R1=5.0 with three comma-separated floats (d_s1,d_s2,d_s3).

outputs.description: Critical crystal fields where first-order transitions occur in the Mn sublattice magnetization.

schema.description: RCP values as a function of reduced external field.

outputs.description: Relative cooling power for different applied magnetic field strengths.

schema.description: RCP values as a function of reduced crystal field.

outputs.description: Relative cooling power for different crystal field values.

schema.description: RCP values as a function of reduced Nd-Mn exchange.

outputs.description: Relative cooling power for different Nd-Mn exchange strengths.

schema.description: RCP values as a function of reduced Mn-Mn exchange.

outputs.description: Relative cooling power for different Mn-Mn exchange strengths.

output_contract.notes: Artifacts are scored based on structural features (plateaus, monotonic trends) and critical field values compared against paper-reported reference (tolerance ±1.0).

steps._comment: Reference plateau definitions are hardcoded in the checker to avoid information leakage.
Gold critical d_s values and tolerance are hardcoded in the checker.
